'''Mouhamed Gueye''' (born 9 November 2002) is a Senegalese [[college basketball]] player for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]]. He moved to the United States as a teenager to play high school basketball at Prolific Prep Academy. Gueye was selected to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first-team as a sophomore with the Cougars in 2023.

==Early life==
Gueye was raised in [[Dakar]], Senegal, as the youngest of four siblings in a sporting family.<ref name=pi>{{cite web |title=Mouhamed Gueye Q&A |url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/mouhamed-gueye |website=Prospective Insight |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=16 April 2021}}</ref><ref name=clark22>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Colton |title='It's always been WSU': Mouhamed Gueye talks offseason, return to Washington State |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2022/jun/15/its-always-been-wsu-mouhamed-gueye-talks-offseason/ |website=The Spokesman-Review |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=15 June 2022}}</ref> He has cousins who have played for the national team and in Europe.<ref name=pi /> Gueye grew up playing [[soccer]] but was encouraged by his mother to play basketball because of his tall height.<ref name=pi /> He credits watching his older brother play basketball as an early influence.<ref name=pi />

==High school career==
Gueye's personal basketball coach, Mamadou Cisse, connected him with Philippe Doherty, the head coach of Prolific Prep Academy in [[Napa, California]].<ref name=pi /> At age 16, he moved from Dakar to the United States to enrol at Prolific Prep.<ref name=clark23>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Colton |title=‘I’m focused on being a pro’: Washington State post Mouhamed Gueye has sights on NBA |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/mar/29/im-focused-on-being-a-pro-washington-state-post-mo/ |website=The Spokesman-Review |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=29 March 2023}}</ref> Gueye had never played organized basketball before playing at Prolific Prep.<ref name=pi />

Gueye emerged as a four-star recruit and a top-50 recruit in the country.<ref name=clark23 /> He completed his academic requirements early and reclassified to the 2021 class before he committed to play for the [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State Cougars]] over several other [[high-major]] offers.<ref name=clark23 /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Lawson |first1=Theo |title=Washington State grabs commitment from Mouhamed Gueye, the highest-ranked recruit in program history |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2021/may/07/washington-state-grabs-commitment-from-mouhamed-gu/ |website=The Spokesman-Review |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=7 May 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
Gueye averaged 7.4 points, 5.2 rebounds and .5 assists per game during his freshman season with the Cougars in 2021–22.<ref name=clark23 /> He was selected to the [[Pac-12]] all-freshman team.<ref name=clark23 /> Gueye declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] but withdrew after receiving insights from franchises.<ref name=clark23 /> He also tested the [[transfer portal]] but elected to return to the Cougars for his sophomore season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Washington State's Mouhamed Gueye withdraws name from men's basketball transfer portal |url=https://www.espn.com.au/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/34052635/washington-state-mouhamed-gueye-withdraws-name-basketball-transfer-portal |website=ESPN |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=7 June 2022}}</ref>

Gueye's role with the Cougars increased during the 2022–23 season following the departures of key pieces in their front-court.<ref name=clark23 /> He also played primarily as a [[Center (basketball)|center]] instead of his natural [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position.<ref name=clark23 /> Gueye was the centrepiece of the Cougars' offense with head coach [[Kyle Smith (basketball)|Kyle Smith]] reinforcing throughout the season that the team "plays through Gueye".<ref name=clark23 /> On 2 February 2023, he scored a career-high 31 points against the [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC Trojans]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ellis sparks Southern Cal past Washington State 80-70 |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-basketball-southern-california-trojans-washington-state-cougars-mens-173c1c19b575c4bfbe9973824666532e |website=AP News |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=3 February 2023}}</ref> Gueye averaged 14.3 points, 8.4 rebounds and 1.9 assists per game during the 2022–23 season and was named to the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first-team.<ref name=clark23 /><ref>{{cite web |title=2022-23 Pac-12 Men's Basketball All-Conference honors and Annual Performance Awards, presented by Nextiva |url=https://pac-12.com/article/2023/03/07/2022-23-pac-12-mens-basketball-all-conference-honors-and-annual-performance |website=Pac-12 |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=7 March 2023}}</ref>

On 4 April 2023, Gueye declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Washington State forward Mouhamed Gueye officially declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2023/apr/04/washington-state-forward-mouhamed-gueye-officially/ |website=The Spokesman-Review |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=4 April 2023}}</ref> He was invited to participate at the [[NBA Draft Combine]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Saglimbeni |first1=Vincent |title=Former local college athletes prepare for next steps in basketball careers |url=https://www.kxly.com/news/former-local-college-athletes-prepare-for-next-steps-in-basketball-careers/article_8f648a4e-ef6d-11ed-807d-1f5f587ef478.html |website=KXLY |access-date=19 May 2023 |date=10 May 2023}}</ref>
